approved: Tax Laws Amendment (2014 Measures No. 1) Bill 2014
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would change rules for farm management deposits, a savings tool farmers use to smooth income when seasons or markets are volatile.

It would let farmers combine deposits held at several banks, increase the off‑farm income they can earn without losing the ability to contribute, and stop bank rules on unclaimed money from applying to these deposits.
A transitional rule would clarify how deposits that became unclaimed money are taxed, applying back to 1 January 2013.
Allows taxpayers to consolidate multiple farm management deposits held with different banks.
Raises the limit on non‑primary production income a taxpayer can receive in a year before being barred from making a deposit.
Prevents the Banking Act's unclaimed‑moneys rules from applying to farm management deposits.
Introduces a transitional rule for the tax treatment of deposits that become unclaimed money, effective from 1 January 2013.
Individuals carrying on a primary production business who use farm management deposits.

Detailed the committee's sixth report covering 18 bills and 175 legislative instruments, and flagged concerns that the G20 (Safety and Security) Complementary Bill 2014 would roll back Commonwealth law at Brisbane Airport during the November G20 summit without a human rights assessment of the Queensland provisions being applied.

Defended the Farm Management Deposits Scheme, noting his Pearce electorate's grain industry exports were worth over $3.1 billion in 2012-13, and disputed opposition examples of budget harm, including on the disability support pension, which supports more than 800,000 Australians, or one in 15 of working age.

Supported the bill, citing $3.2 billion currently held in Farm Management Deposit accounts nationally, including about $200 million across 2,000 beef sector participants, and explained the amendment raises the off-farm income threshold from $65,000 to $100,000 and allows consolidation of deposits up to $400,000.

Supported the bill, noting the GST self-assessment measure will cost $4 million over the forward estimates, described dairy farmers in his electorate spending up to $30,000 a month on grain during dry conditions, and welcomed raising the Farm Management Deposits threshold from $65,000 to $100,000.

Closed debate on the bill, summarising three amendments improving the Farm Management Deposits Scheme and GST provisions allowing taxpayers to self-assess refund entitlements, and confirmed the government would not support the opposition's amendment.
